So born on the Piedmont, now in Delmarva -- the very north, but not as far as Wilmington. 

There are huge cultural divides from place to place: Newark? Typical college town; the beach towns? Standard East Coast; the further down you go, it is VERY rural -- great farmland; the Eastern Shore is beautiful - small towns right on the water -- wonderful week drive in summer.

The Virginia beach segments & barrier islands are stunning & worth a visit -- camping is the best way to go, but spots are reserved early in the year for summer travel. Be prepared for 1. Beach/island horses & 2. Mammoth swarms of flies (especially with winds from the west).

comments.author: @nancyhaddon4996
comments.text: English settlement on Delmarva began in 1614 on Plantation Creek near Cape Charles, Va, where Sir Thomas Dale sent colonists over from Jamestown to establish a saltworks. Prior to English settlement, the area was inhabited by the indigenous Accawmacke ( Accomack) tribe. Early correspondence between England and Jamestown was addressed to the colonists of Jamestown, and "Ye Kingdome of Accawmacke", which is the current Cape Charles area. The first reservation was also established in this area, called the "Gingaskin Reservation".
